AcePolicyGate.description:
How the ACE engine treated the call at the moment a policy run completed.

`PolicyEngine.run` emits the SAME `PolicyRunComplete`, with the same
fields, whether (a) the policy chain was EMPTY and the target default
allowed, (b) a policy returned `Allowed`, or (c) every policy returned
`Continue` and the default allowed. So the event proves the target was
attached, `run` was called, and the call was not rejected — it does NOT
prove that any policy evaluated anything. Without this field the three
collapse onto one "a policy run exists" label, and a fail-open gate reads
as screened.

The vocabulary is deliberately the one the router provisioner already uses
for the same question (`workspace_routers::onchain::AceEntryGate`), minus
`Refused`: a refused call reverts and emits no `PolicyRunComplete`, so it
is structurally impossible for a RECORDED run and is not representable
here by construction.

the backend had already done. `lifecycle::apply_transition` captures the
delivered amount on the settle transition and `orders` stores it; every

deliveredOutputProvenance.description:

back from settlement evidence (a receipt-backed bridge delivery, a
realized DEX output, a Circle-settled FX output, a deferred settlement's
executed amount), `"quoted"` when a quote-time value was carried forward
because nothing measured the delivery.

This field is the whole point of the pair. The lifecycle falls back to
the quoted output when no measurement exists, which makes "measured,
zero slippage" and "never measured" byte-identical — `realizedSlippageBps`
reads 0 for both and the delivered column repeats the quote. A client
that renders a delivered amount without reading this is reporting a
quote as a receipt.

realizedSlippageBps.description:
Realized adverse slippage in basis points, computed at settlement as

means the delivery beat the quote.

Deliberately NOT named `slippageBps`: this struct already carries
`slippageToleranceBps`, which is the tolerance the order was SUBMITTED
with — a quote-time input, not an outcome. Two fields one word apart
that mean "what I allowed" and "what I got" is how a caller ends up
charting the limit as the result, so the outcome names itself.

them lives in the backend's registry-derived catalogue — a client that
cannot find the token has no way to scale the number and ends up
printing base units as a human quantity (a Solana leg rendered
`940,000` for 0.94 PYUSD). `resolutionStatus` states honestly whether
the backend resolved the asset; when it is `unknown`, `decimals` and
`decimalAmount` are absent rather than guessed.

Purely additive: `inputAmounts`/`outputAmounts` are unchanged, and
`rawAmount` here repeats their value verbatim. Always serialized;

QuoteSourceEntry.description:
One considered venue's outcome, a closed set tagged `status`:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `asking` | in flight on the stream only: the auction is consulting this venue now; its final outcome replaces it under the same venue key, and none remains at `complete` |
| `answered` | the venue produced a quote |
| `needsWallet` | no wallet of `family` to ask with |
| `walletRefused` | the bound wallet is refused (`Revoked`, a confirmed sanctions hit) |
| `firmQuoteLimited` | a desk's firm-quote cap applies; `explanation` is product copy |
| `priceOnRequest` | no venue price was requested; `quoteId` identifies the held estimate or stub to Requote |
| `askLimitReached` | the venue's ask limit is reached for now; `retryAfter` says when to ask again |
| `timedOut` | no answer inside the deadline |
| `refused` | the venue refused the live ask |
| `restricted` | a gate kept the venue from this principal |
| `unsupported` | the venue does not serve the pair |
| `filteredOut` | the request's own filters exclude it (never a coverage or chain gap) |
| `unavailable` | a read failed (`kybUnavailable`, `admissionUnavailable`, …) |

An unscreened default wallet is not a status: the quote carries `screening`. `venue`
is the venue block, its `id` the one quote legs and `/prices` rows carry. Durations
(`retryAfter`) are ISO 8601, counted from when the response was sent. Every entry
carries `asked`: whether this venue was consulted for this request: a live ask, or a
fresh read of its published book or live desk price within that source's freshness
window. An estimate no venue gave (a model or reference price) is not consulted, and
an `answered` entry is always consulted. How a card's price was obtained is its own
price basis, never this flag.

Ask for the permission or wallet right `target`. For a member session it is offered only
when the permission-request owner would open (or already holds) a request on it; a target
it refuses by name (`blocked`, `not_applicable`, ...) reads `none`. When that read fails,
the step is offered unchanged.

The calling member's own pending request for this same target (the target key
the create route deduplicates on, so a request made from another venue's card
counts), read once per auction: the member already asked, so a client shows that
instead of offering a second request. Absent when there is none, when the read
failed or timed out (never a guessed value), and always for API keys and
automation principals: only a member session's quotes carry it.

TetraFi is an API for institutional trading across on-chain and off-chain venues: discover assets, request quotes, place an order by quote id and read its status. API keys sign every request.

post.description: Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A venue (Basic) quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`); a protocol (Advanced) quote becomes a protocol order (`advancedTrade`), after POST /orders/preflight and any wallet signature or source transaction it asks for. Each quote is ordered once: the same quote again answers QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, and a replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer. Read what a quote produced with GET /orders/by-quote/{quoteId}.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. Refusals are not stored: after one, fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.

post.description: The asset-pair contract (PairQuoteRequest or RequoteRequest); the legacy intent body is retired, so an object without `pay` or `requote` is 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming `pay`. Validated in order (INVALID_REQUEST naming the field, REQUOTE_FIELDS_CONFLICT, UNKNOWN_ASSET / UNKNOWN_CHAIN / UNKNOWN_VENUE naming the value, ASSET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a side's Asset has no deployment on the chain pinned for it), INVALID_AMOUNT, SAME_ASSET_NEEDS_CHAIN, CHAIN_PIN_NEEDS_ON_CHAIN, out-of-range INVALID_REQUEST, ROUTING_OPTIONS_FORBIDDEN), then the request_quotes capability, and answered with a PairQuoteSet: every venue planned, venue-hitting plans limited to one every 3 s per principal (429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; cache-only plans are not limited), quotes held for their owner and the set recorded for GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId}. A requote body asks only the earlier quote's venue again (every venue of a multi-leg route, which answers that same route), as JSON (never a stream), and answers a PairQuoteSet whose one quote names it in requoteOf; the earlier quote stays held until its own expiry. Requote refusals: 400 CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED / BINDING_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a custody vault or registered workspace address bound to a chain it is not an account of; also on a fresh request), 403 SOURCE_NOT_OWNED / ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE / VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL, 404 QUOTE_NOT_FOUND (unknown and another principal's quote alike), 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED (details.reason) / REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET / PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED / QUOTE_CANNOT_BE_REFRESHED (a quote recorded before it could be refreshed for a broker's client), 410 QUOTE_EXPIRED (10 minutes after its expiry), 429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED / VENUE_FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED /BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, 503 QUOTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE / QUOTE_NOT_READY, 504 REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT. Every refusal, at every status, is the one error body ApiError {error, message, requestId, timestamp, next?, details?}. Optional filters narrow the auction. Orderable venue-account cards require a current MFA human Company/Broker session, or an API key holding workspace_venue_trade with its venue switch enabled and HMAC request signing. A member key with quotes_request but no venue-trading authority receives native indicative cards (commitment.kind indicative) with sourceRefusal venueTradeScopeRequired and a re-issuance remedy, without any firm ask. On-chain sources without an organisation wallet grant are indicative with sourceRefusal onchainWalletNotUsable and a wallet-grant remedy; no signer is resolved. Quote-only observations never spend firm-quote budget, and their held refusal is returned if ordered. An API key quotes with quotes_request (which needs orders_write on the same key); it has no Default wallet of a member, so it binds a workspace wallet in bind.wallets: a workspace custody wallet, or an organisation wallet the key was granted (without that grant the source reads API_KEY_ORGANISATION_WALLET_SCOPE_REQUIRED), never a personal one (409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED); its protocol venues remain non-orderable until it binds one; quote-only observations may show a native indicative price without borrowing a wallet. A desk on a production site is firm-asked only on request, the same for sessions and API keys, each one call: name it in filters.venues.include and its firm quote returns in that response, or requote its indicative card ({requote: quoteId}). A broad request never asks it: its card stays indicative and reads unavailable priceOnRequest when it publishes no price. Its next is requote, except where its firm quote lives 5 s or less: then it is order (execute within my limit), and that order makes the one ask, trading only at or above the person's minReceive; a requote of that card (Get firm quote) also asks it once under the same desk limits and returns a firm, executable card with its expiresAt. A sandbox or testnet desk that publishes nothing is firm-asked on a person's or API caller's request within the desk limits (firmQuoteLimited with retryAfter when they are reached); automation principals get it on requote only. On a venue-account card, bind.deliverTo {kind: address, chain, address, destinationTag?} names where the trade's output is withdrawn when the order for it fills: one of the workspace's own wallets that is an approved withdrawal destination of that venue account, for the receipt asset, with exactly that destination tag or memo. The card then carries that deliverTo, a network fee line for the venue's withdrawal fee (the most the order will pay; a higher fee at send refuses) and a receive net of it (netReceived unavailable withdrawalFeeUnread when the fee could not be read), and a requote keeps it. A venue that cannot deliver there answers its source unavailable with DESTINATION_NOT_APPROVED, DELIVER_TO_NOT_A_WORKSPACE_WALLET, WITHDRAWAL_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED (no withdrawal network for that chain on the site; test sites have none), DELIVER_TO_AMBIGUOUS, WITHDRAWAL_FEE_EXCEEDS_AMOUNT, deliverToCalldataUnsupported or deliverToNotPermitted (deliverTo needs a member session with ViewWallets; an API key lists no deliverTo candidates, and a requote naming one answers 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED with details.reason deliverToNotPermitted). The request spends one Quote token; connection indicative pacing is reported on cards.
